# Taskscape: the feature list

1598 features of the reference app in 19 areas. Each was found independently from the code (A) and from recordings of the running app or its docs (B), merged, then checked for exactness against both.

Pixel sizes: the reference sets the root font size to 14px, so 1rem = 14px and a Tailwind class like h-8 is 28px.

## 1. Task list (85 features)

**F01-001 · Search field placeholder and leading icon**
- *Trigger:* none (observed in each pane's header)
- *When:* Always visible at the top of every pane. The search icon is the leading element of the input well, at the left of the field; the placeholder text starts to the right of the icon. Value is empty in every recording.
- *Result:* The empty search field shows the placeholder 'Search {list name}' (for example 'Search Inbox' or 'Search Errands'), with a search icon (size 18, weight 300) on its left.
- *Exact:* placeholder = `Search {list.name}`; leading icon = `search, size 18, weight 300`; input well (recorded) = `InputWell mx-4 mt-3 mb-2 h-10 shrink-0, measured 832x35 at @14,56`
- *Status:* corrected, found by A+B
- *Check notes:* Both checkers corrected the context. A verified the code: a leading Icon search (size 18, weight 300) and the placeholder `Search ${list.name}`. B's recordings show the icon at x=23 and the TextInput placeholder at x=46 ('Search Errands' in main-default, 'Search Inbox' in empty-list), so the placeholder sits to the right of the icon. The feature's 'left of the search icon' wording is contradicted by the tree. Recorded InputWell 832x35 @14,56 agrees in both. Empty value is confirmed in every tree (B) but cannot be checked from code (A).
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:204-213, state:main-default (tree.txt lines 35-37), state:empty-list (tree.txt lines 29-31), state:new-task-added (TaskPane > InputWell, TextInput2 placeholder), state:multi-select-shift (TaskPane > InputWell), main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:204-213 (InputWell className "mx-4 mt-3 mb-2 h-10 shrink-0", leading Icon search size 18 weight 300, placeholder `Search ${list.name}`). Recorded 832x35 @14,56 and the empty-value claim cannot be checked from code., Placeholder and icon: spec/references/main-default/tree.txt:36-37 (Icon search size=18 weight=300 at x=23; TextInput2 placeholder="Search Errands" at x=46). spec/references/empty-list/tree.txt:31 placeholder="Search Inbox". InputWell mx-4 mt-3 mb-2 h-10 shrink-0 @14,56 832x35 at main-default/tree.txt:35. value="" on TextInput2 in every tree. The context sentence 'left of the search icon' contradicts the tree: the icon is at x=23 and the text input starts at x=46, so the placeholder is to the right of the icon.

**F01-002 · Typing filters the pane's task tree**
- *Trigger:* Typing in the pane's search field
- *When:* Pane search field has focus; query is non-empty after trimming whitespace
- *Result:* Root tasks are filtered by visibility in the pane. While a query is active, every subtask group is shown expanded, even subtasks the user collapsed. Whitespace-only input does not count as a search.
- *Exact:* searching condition = `query.trim().length > 0`
- *Edge cases:* Collapsed subtask groups stay collapsed in the store; they re-collapse when the query is cleared (expanded is computed as searching || !collapsedHere).
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A verified the wiring in TaskPane.tsx and TaskRow.tsx (query state, searching flag, visibleRoots, expanded rule). The query-matching rule in stores/visibility and searchStore was not read. B found no recording with a non-empty query, so the behaviour is not observable from recordings.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:67, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:75-80, main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:89-90, main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:110, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:67, 75-80 (query, searching = query.trim().length > 0, visibleRoots); main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:89-90, 110 (expanded: searching || !collapsedHere). The query-matching itself lives in stores/visibility and searchStore, which are outside the allowed files, so the exact match rule was not verified., No recording has a non-empty pane query: TextInput2 value="" in every tree.txt (e.g. main-default/tree.txt:37). The filter and the expanded-while-searching behaviour are not observable from these recordings. Source was not read, per the task.

**F01-005 · Escape in search field clears the search and leaves the field**
- *Trigger:* Press Escape while the search field has focus
- *When:* Search field focused (query may be empty or not)
- *Result:* The query is cleared and the field loses focus (blur). The key event does not propagate further.
- *Exact:* key = `Escape`
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A verified Escape handling in source (searchStore.clear then blur, after stopPropagation). B found only IPC command names in meta.json, no key events, so Escape is not observable from recordings.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:217-221, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:217-221 (e.key === 'Escape' -> searchStore.clear(list.id) then target.blur()); line 218 e.stopPropagation() runs first on every keydown., meta.json command lists contain only IPC calls (get_setting, list_lists, all_tasks, boot_done, etc.), no key events. Escape handling is not observable from any folder.

**F01-006 · Enter cycles forward through matches**
- *Trigger:* Press Enter while the search field has focus
- *When:* Query has at least one direct match in the pane
- *Result:* Focus moves to the next match in visual order (wrapping from last to first). The preview selects that task, and the row scrolls into view with block nearest.
- *Exact:* key = `Enter`; scroll behaviour = `scrollIntoView block nearest`
- *Edge cases:* If no row is currently focused, Enter goes to the first match. · Wrap-around is computed as (at + dir + length) % length.
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A verified cycleMatch in source: Enter cycles to the next direct match, a missing focused row gives index -1 so Enter selects the first match, and scrollIntoView uses block 'nearest'. B found no key events in recordings.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:174-194, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:222, main/src/lib/scroll.ts:4-7, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:174-194 (cycleMatch; returns if direct.size === 0; ordered = flattenVisible filtered to direct matches; nextId = ordered[(at + dir + ordered.length) % ordered.length]; focus(nextId); scrollTaskIntoView); line 222 (Enter -> cycleMatch(1)); main/src/lib/scroll.ts:4-7 (scrollIntoView block 'nearest'). With no focused row, at = -1 so Enter yields ordered[0]., No key events recorded in meta.json command lists. Enter cycling, selection and scroll are not observable. Only the multi-select folders set active lists and no search query is present in any tree.

**F01-007 · Shift+Enter cycles backward through matches**
- *Trigger:* Press Shift+Enter while the search field has focus
- *When:* Query has at least one direct match in the pane
- *Result:* Focus moves to the previous match in visual order (wrapping from first to last). Same selection and scroll as Enter.
- *Exact:* keys = `Shift+Enter`
- *Edge cases:* When no row is focused, Shift+Enter with the formula (-1 - 1 + length) % length lands on the second-to-last match rather than the last one.
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A verified the Shift+Enter formula (direction -1 gives the second-to-last match when no row is focused). Edge case from A: with a single match, (len - 2 + 1) % 1 resolves to index 0, so the only match is selected and 'second-to-last' does not apply. B found no Shift+Enter key event in recordings.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:174-194, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:222, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:222 (e.shiftKey ? -1 : 1), 190-191 (formula). With no focused row and dir -1, index is (len - 2) % len, i.e. second-to-last, as stated. For a single match the result is that match., No Shift+Enter key event in meta.json command lists. Backward cycling and its edge case are not observable.

**F01-008 · Search keystrokes do not reach global handlers**
- *Trigger:* Any key pressed while the search field has focus
- *When:* Search field focused
- *Result:* Key events are stopped at the search field, so pane-level or app-level shortcuts do not fire while typing a query.
- *Exact:* behaviour = `e.stopPropagation() on every keydown in the search field`
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A verified that the search input's onKeyDown calls e.stopPropagation() before any key check. Window-level capture-phase listeners were not checked because no global handler code is in the allowed files. B found no key events and no search query in any tree.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:217-218, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:217-218 (onKeyDown calls e.stopPropagation() before any key check). Whether window-level capture-phase listeners are affected was not verified, because no global handler code is in the allowed files., Propagation of keydown is not observable. No key events in meta.json and no search query in any tree.

**F01-020 · Drop dragged tasks on blank pane space to move them to the list root**
- *Trigger:* Drag one or more task rows over blank area of the task list (not over a row) and release
- *When:* Drag payload type application/x-task

**F01-021 · Auto-scroll while dragging near the top or bottom edge**
- *Trigger:* Hold a task drag so the pointer sits within 56px of the pane's top or bottom edge
- *When:* Dragging a task (draggingId set) inside the pane's bounding box
- *Result:* The pane scrolls up or down each animation frame, with speed rising linearly to 16px per frame at the edge. Scrolling continues while the pointer stays still, and stops on drop, dragend, or leaving the zone.
- *Exact:* speed formula = `Near top: speed = -Math.ceil(((EDGE - topGap) / EDGE) * MAX) (scrolls up, negative). Near bottom: speed = +Math.ceil(((EDGE - botGap) / EDGE) * MAX) (scrolls down, positive). Zero outside the pane's bounding box or outside the 56px zones.`
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* A corrected the speed formula from source (TaskPane.tsx:117-161; EDGE 56, MAX 16). Edge case from A: leaving the zone sets speed to 0 only when the next dragover event fires (lines 138-144); stop() on drop, dragend and cleanup ends the loop (lines 147-154). B found auto-scroll during drag is not recorded; long-list-scrolled shows a scroll offset only, with no drag.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:112-161, main/src/components/TaskPane.tsx:117-161 (EDGE = 56 at line 120; MAX = 16 at line 121; speed at 138-144; tick at 124-127; stop on drop/dragend at 153-154, 147-151)., Auto-scroll during drag is not recorded. long-list-scrolled/tree.txt shows a scroll offset (rows at y=-802 at line 44), but no drag, so the speed and edge zone cannot be checked.

**F01-034 · Task row anatomy: check, title, note line, More button**
- *Trigger:* none (static layout observed in every state)

**F01-084 · Inline subtask composer keys: Enter adds, empty Enter or Escape or blur dismisses, and keys do not reach global handlers**
- *Trigger:* A row's inline subtask composer is open (opened via the row menu's Add subtask), and the user types in its input, presses Enter or Escape, or moves focus away.
- *When:* The composer is a TextInput rendered under the row with placeholder 'Subtask title — Enter to add'. Its onKeyDown calls e.stopPropagation() first, so keystrokes never reach the window-level useAppKeyboard map. Enter with a non-empty trimmed value calls onSubmit(title) and clears the field, so the composer stays open for the next subtask. Enter with an empty value calls onDismiss(). Escape calls onDismiss(). onBlur also calls onDismiss(). The index only has F09-050 (one composer open at a time), which does not cover these keys.
- *Result:* Enter with text submits a subtask and keeps the composer open with an empty field. Enter on an empty field, Escape, or losing focus closes the composer without creating anything. Global shortcuts such as Escape-clears-selection or Delete do not fire while the composer has focus.
- *Exact:* Composer placeholder text = `Subtask title — Enter to add`; Enter with trimmed non-empty title = `onSubmit(title), then the input value is set to empty and the composer stays open`; Enter with empty or whitespace-only title = `onDismiss() (composer closes)`; Escape = `onDismiss()`; Blur = `onBlur={onDismiss}`; Keydown propagation = `e.stopPropagation() before key handling`
- *Status:* confirmed by review, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Reviewed by Mujtaba (2026-11-13): true. Earlier check: Checker B could not check: no recording shows the subtask composer, its placeholder, or its key and blur handling. Checker A did not check this item.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:604-620, main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:606, main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:607-617, No checker A entry for this feature., No folder shows an open inline subtask composer or the placeholder 'Subtask title — Enter to add'. I read all nine tree.txt files and none contains that placeholder. new-task-draft/tree.txt:96-108 is the DraftInspector for a new task, not the subtask composer. Key handling and blur cannot be seen in any recording.

## 2. Title bar and navigation (63 features)

**F02-001 · Double-click the title bar background to maximize or restore the window**
- *Trigger:* Double-click on the header's empty area (the element itself must carry the data-tauri-drag-region attribute)
- *When:* Any time the main window is open; header is the title bar
- *Result:* Calls getCurrentWindow().toggleMaximize(). Double-clicks on interactive children (project pill, tabs, buttons) do not trigger it because the target must itself have the drag-region attribute.
- *Exact:* Header height class = `h-13`; Header bottom border classes (light/dark) = `border-edge-2l / dark:border-edge-2d`; Header background classes (light/dark) = `bg-surface-1l / dark:bg-surface-1d`
- *Edge cases:* The drag-indicator slot (TitleBar.tsx:52) carries data-tauri-drag-region, so a double-click on it also toggles maximize. · The trailing empty strip in ListTabs (ListTabs.tsx:303) also carries the attribute, so a double-click there toggles maximize. · Non-mac spacer span className="w-3" (TitleBar.tsx:49) and the view-controls wrapper (TitleBar.tsx:64) have no drag-region attribute, so a double-click there does nothing.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A, OS integration
- *Check notes:* Checker B could not check (no double-click recorded, no source read). Checker A's edge cases are source-derived and adopted as is.
- *Sources:* main/src/components/TitleBar.tsx:41-47, main/src/components/TitleBar.tsx:41-47 (header has data-tauri-drag-region, onDoubleClick checks e.target hasAttribute data-tauri-drag-region then getCurrentWindow().toggleMaximize(); classes h-13, border-edge-2l dark:border-edge-2d, bg-surface-1l dark:bg-surface-1d all match). Drag-region attribute also on the drag-indicator slot at TitleBar.tsx:52 and on the trailing strip at main/src/components/ListTabs.tsx:303., No double-click is recorded in any of the nine meta.json files (commands are only boot/list/setting calls). tree.txt line 2 shows TitleBar @0,0 1180x46 in all states, so the rendered header is 46px tall, but the class-to-pixel mapping for h-13 and the border/background classes are not in any tree. data-tauri-drag-region is not shown in the trees. **F02-006 · Dismiss the project dropdown with Escape or a press outside, but not by re-pressing the pill**

**F02-058 · Tab strip scrolls horizontally with a hidden scrollbar**

**F03-028 · New note is created on first keystroke and streams saves**
- *Trigger:* type into the new note editor
- *When:* Add-note editor open
- *Result:* Each change restarts a 500 ms debounce, so the note is created on the backend after a 500 ms pause. **F04-038 · Derived display name for a linked reference**
- *Trigger:* none (applied when a link is added)
- *When:* The parse-failure fallback (raw value) applies only to the remote branch (AttachmentSection.tsx:26-29). The local branch never parses a URL.
- *Result:* For an http or https value, the name is the last non-empty path segment, or the host when the path is empty. For a local path, it is the last segment split on / or \\. If parsing fails the raw value is used.
- *Exact:* local rule fallback = `|| location (raw value when no non-empty segment)`
- *Edge cases:* A local value with no non-empty segment (for example '/') falls back to the raw value (AttachmentSection.tsx:32). · The remote check uses trimmed input (fileKind.ts:119), but new URL() is called on the untrimmed location (AttachmentSection.tsx:26).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Sources:* main/src/components/preview/AttachmentSection.tsx:23-33, A: AttachmentSection.tsx:23-33 (referenceName). Remote branch :24-30 uses url.pathname.split('/').filter(Boolean).pop() || url.host and returns location on URL parse failure (:28-29). Local branch :32 is location.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean).pop() || location., B: No reference records a linked reference being added or a derived name shown. No recording of link names beyond 'Brand brief' (attachment-menu/shot.png), which does not show the derivation rule.

- *Result:* The name is split into base and extension. Only an alphanumeric suffix of 1 to 10 characters after a dot that is not the first character counts as an extension; otherwise the whole name is the base. The extension keeps its case.
- *Exact:* dot rule = `only the last dot is considered (lastIndexOf); it must be at index > 0 and not the final character`
- *Edge cases:* Names like example.com/page or dotfiles stay whole. · A trailing dot leaves the name whole.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* B could not check. A's dot rule is adopted from the code. The extension regex (/^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,10}$/) and case-preserving ext from A's evidence are retained as stated.
- *Sources:* common-ui/src/fileKind.ts:105-116, A: fileKind.ts:108-116 splitFileName: uses lastIndexOf('.') (:110), requires dot > 0 (:111, first char excluded) and dot < length-1 (trailing dot leaves name whole), ext must match /^[A-Za-z0-9]{1,10}$/ (:113), ext keeps case (:112-113)., B: No rename prompt is recorded in any reference, so the base and extension split cannot be seen.

**F04-071 · Local attachment file location resolution**
- *Trigger:* none (used by thumbnails and lightbox sources)
- *When:* Attachment path resolution
- *Result:* A copied attachment (link_type copy) resolves to join(homeDir(), '.taskscape', location) regardless of remote-looking text (fileKind.ts:154-155). For other link types the location is trimmed, then: http(s) (case-insensitive) resolves to null; a file:// location is decoded with decodeURI (fileKind.ts:158); a location starting with / or a drive letter is used as is (fileKind.ts:159); anything else resolves to null. attachmentSrc wraps the resolved path with convertFileSrc for webview use (fileKind.ts:164-166). Null means no thumbnail (AttachmentSection.tsx:56-57) and the lightbox shows 'No inline preview' (AttachmentLightbox.tsx:224).
- *Exact:* location trim = `trim() is applied for non-copy links before the remote, file:// and absolute tests; the copy branch uses the untrimmed location (fileKind.ts:156 vs 154-155)`; file scheme decode = `decodeURI(loc.slice('file://'.length)) (fileKind.ts:158); decodeURI, not decodeURIComponent`; remote test = `/^https?:\/\//i on the trimmed location (fileKind.ts:119)`; web asset conversion = `convertFileSrc(path) from @tauri-apps/api/core (fileKind.ts:1, 166)`
- *Edge cases:* A link_type of copy with an http(s) location still resolves to the home path (fileKind.ts:154-155), so it can produce a thumbnail if it is an image kind.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A, OS integration
- *Check notes:* B could not check the resolution rules; the corrections come from A's source reading. B's screenshot shows the two tile kinds but not the rules.
- *Sources:* common-ui/src/fileKind.ts:152-167, A: common-ui/src/fileKind.ts:118-119 (isRemote), 152-167 (attachmentPath, attachmentSrc); AttachmentSection.tsx:55-57; AttachmentLightbox.tsx:101-102, 224, B: No source code was read, so the path rules cannot be checked. meta.json files show only plugin:path|resolve_directory and plugin:path|join calls with no arguments (spec/references/attachment-lightbox/meta.json:34-41; inspector-notes/meta.json:35-38; attachment-menu/meta.json:35-38). shot shows a link-icon tile 'Brand brief' and an image tile 'hero-sketch.png' (inspector-notes/shot.png).

**F04-118 · Draft with no title: commit or click-away discards the draft without writing a row, and the Untitled fallback applies only to note, shot, and screenshot actions**
- *Trigger:* User leaves the new-task draft title empty and presses Enter (commit) or clicks away from the draft.
- *When:* runDraftAction returns early on a commit with an empty trimmed title and only clears the draft. The DraftInspector comment says click-away with no title drops the draft and nothing is written. Index F04-003 and F04-005 cover commit and click-away only for a non-empty title. The fallback title 'Untitled' is reached only by note, shot, and screenshot actions.
- *Result:* The draft is dropped silently: no task row is created and no error or toast is shown.
- *Exact:* Trimmed title check that discards the draft on commit = `if (action === 'commit' && !title) return ui.setDraftListId(null);`; Action that creates the task with the fallback title 'Untitled' when the title is empty = `action === 'commit' ? title : title || 'Untitled' (only note, shot, and screenshot actions reach the fallback)`
- *Status:* confirmed by review, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Reviewed by Mujtaba (2026-11-13): true, but only while nothing has been added to the draft: adding a note or a screenshot creates the task (as "Untitled" if it has no title), so there is nothing left to discard. Code agrees: commands/tasks.ts:182 discards an empty commit; :195 creates "Untitled" for note and shot. Earlier check: Neither checker could verify this item. A has no entry for F04-118. B could not check because the cited code is source that its audit does not read. No recorded commit, click-away, created row or toast is in the spec folders. The 'Untitled' heading is a placeholder, not a stored title.
- *Sources:* main/src/commands/tasks.ts:181-182, main/src/commands/tasks.ts:193-196, main/src/components/preview/DraftInspector.tsx:16-17, main/src/components/preview/DraftInspector.tsx:56, The cited code locations (taskscape-tauri/main/src/commands/tasks.ts and DraftInspector.tsx) are source code, which this audit does not read. The spec folders do not record a commit with an empty title, a click-away, or any created row or toast. new-task-draft/shot.png and new-task-typed/shot.png show the draft inspector with the grey heading 'Untitled' and a 'Start with' Note and Screenshot panel. That heading is a placeholder display, not a created task, and it does not show whether 'Untitled' is used as a stored title.

**F04-119 · Draft action guard prevents a single action from creating two task rows**
- *Trigger:* A second draft action (commit, note, shot, or the unmount blur) fires while the first is still running.
- *When:* A module-level draftBusy flag makes runDraftAction return early while an action is in flight. The comment says it swallows the DraftInspector unmount blur, which would otherwise commit again as the form tears down. The flag is reset in a finally block.
- *Result:* Only one task row is created per draft action. Re-entrant calls are ignored with no feedback.
- *Exact:* Guard flag and early return = `let draftBusy = false; ... if (!listId || draftBusy) return; ... finally { draftBusy = false; }`
- *Status:* confirmed in code, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Verified in code by the orchestrator: commands/tasks.ts:167-205. A module-level draftBusy flag makes runDraftAction return early while an action is running; it exists to swallow the extra "commit" fired by the draft inspector's blur as it unmounts, so one action creates one row. Earlier check: Neither checker could verify this item. A has no entry for F04-119. B could not check because the draftBusy guard is source code it does not read. No recorded state shows two draft actions firing or a row count after one action.

**F05-027 · Search query per pane turns filtering on**
- *Trigger:* type into the pane's search field (UI not in these files)

**F06-007 · ArrowDown moves highlight down**
- *Trigger:* ArrowDown in the palette input
- *When:* Palette open; results present

**F06-037 · Palette ArrowDown with no results leaves the highlight at -1**
- *Trigger:* ArrowDown in the palette input
- *When:* Palette open; query matches no command
- *Result:* ArrowDown computes Math.min(a + 1, results.length - 1). With no results this is Math.min(a + 1, -1), which gives -1. runAt(-1) returns without running anything, and no row is highlighted. Typing resets the highlight to 0.
- *Exact:* computed index = `Math.min(a + 1, results.length - 1)`

**F07-015 · Undo stack records each command**

**F07-039 · Drop a task on a row (before / after)**
- *Trigger:* Drag a task onto the top or bottom area of another row (drag zone detection in other area)
- *When:* dropOnRow with zone 'before' or 'after'; target not inside dragged subtree
- *Result:* Dragged task is placed adjacent to target among siblings (dragged row excluded from the sibling list). Sort value is the midpoint of the two neighbours. With no previous sibling it is the next sibling's sort minus 1000; with no next sibling it is the previous sibling's sort plus 1000. If both neighbours exist and are less than 1 apart, the whole sibling group is rebuilt in one undoable 'Move' at (i+1)*1000 steps, with the dragged row inserted in its new slot.
- *Exact:* spacing = `1000`; rebuild threshold = `< 1`
- *Edge cases:* When the target is the only sibling (no previous and no next), the sort is the target's sort minus 1000 (actions.ts:263). · The rebuild threshold check (< 1) applies only when both a previous and a next sibling exist (actions.ts:250).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* Checker A corrected the before/after drop placement and sort math against source. Checker B could not check (no before/after drop recorded). Source decides, so A's correction stands.
- *Sources:* main/src/stores/actions.ts:222-267, main/src/stores/actions.ts:250-267. Threshold check '< 1' at line 250 only runs when both prev and next exist; start/end/only-sibling sort math at lines 262-265., No reference records a before/after drop or sort values. **F08-001 · Global shortcuts are suspended while a sheet is open**

- *When:* Sheet overlay (useSheetStore.current set)
- *Result:* The global keyboard map returns immediately; the sheet owns the keyboard.

- *Edge cases:* Sheet's own Escape/Enter handling lives in SheetHost.tsx, outside this area.
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* Checker A verified the guard in source. Checker B could not check it from recordings.
- *Sources:* main/src/hooks/useAppKeyboard.ts:43-46, useAppKeyboard.ts:43-46 (sheet guard `if (useSheetStore.getState().current) return;`)., No reference shows a sheet open. Every tree.txt ends with an empty SheetHost (e.g. spec/references/rename-inline/tree.txt:100, spec/references/option-held/tree.txt:127). The guard source was not read, per instructions.

**F09-007 · Creating a project does not go through setActive (pane and persistence side effects)**
- *Trigger:* Create a project from the New project sheet (see the Create a new project entry)
- *When:* Any project creation
- *Result:* projectStore.create sets the active id directly with set(), so api.setActiveProject is not called and last_active_project is not updated, so a relaunch restores the previous project. - *Status:* confirmed by one, found by critic
- *Check notes:* Confirmed by checker A from source (create() sets activeId directly, bypassing setActive, and does not reset panes). Checker B found no reference showing project creation.
- *Sources:* main/src/stores/projectStore.ts:46-51, main/src/commands/projects.ts:12-22, main/src/App.tsx:40, projectStore.ts:46-51: create() calls set({ activeId: project.id }) directly, then load() and list load; it does not call setActive (projectStore.ts:41-44, the only path that calls api.setActiveProject). Left pane is not reset: create() does not call resetForProject (layoutStore.ts:131-139). Empty-state title for zero lists is at App.tsx:96-98 ('No lists yet' when the new project has no lists), consistent with the inferred result., No reference shows project creation, setActive side effects, last_active_project persistence, or pane state after creating a project. sheet-new-project/meta.json has no set_active_project call.

**F09-010 · Deleting a list reconciles both panes (fallback to the first remaining list)**
- *Trigger:* Confirm delete on a list
- *When:* Runs after the list is removed, with the set of valid list ids in the active project. Applies to both panes; the focused/active or split list may have been the deleted one.
- *Result:* The left pane keeps its list if still valid; if it showed the deleted list it is re-pointed to the first list of the active project, or cleared to null if the project has no lists left, so the view never lands on the No lists yet state while lists exist. The split pane keeps its list only if the list still exists and is not the same as the left pane's list; otherwise the split closes (split list set to null) and ui.split is removed from localStorage. Focus keeps its list if valid, otherwise goes to the left pane's list. ui.split is removed if no split remains.
- *Exact:* fallback (left pane) = `first list in the active project, else null`; storage key removed = `ui.split`
- *Edge cases:* Split pane keeps its list only if it still exists and is not the same as the active pane's list · If the split pane's list is removed the split closes and ui.split is removed from localStorage
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* Confirmed by checker A from source (reconcileLists and layoutStore.ts:141-157 fallback logic). Checker B found no reference showing a list deletion or the resulting pane state.
- *Sources:* main/src/commands/lists.ts:79-89, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:141-157, lists.ts:79-89: reconcileLists(new Set(inProject ids), inProject[0]?.id ?? null) after remove; layoutStore.ts:141-157: keep(activeListId) ?? fallbackId (144); split kept only if valid and not equal to the new activeListId (145-148), else null; focus keep(paneFocus) ?? activeListId (152); line 155 removes 'ui.split' when no split remains., No reference shows a list deletion (sheet-delete-list/meta.json has no delete_list or reload commands) or the post-delete pane state.

**F09-016 · Switch to another project resets the panes**
- *Trigger:* Invoke selectProject(id) (trigger wired outside this area); in the recording, choose 'Spring launch' in the project menu (inferred from the commands sent)
- *When:* Any project switch

Event listeners, layout reconcile and veil dismissal are not recorded.

**F09-037 · Boot veil fade-out timing**
- *Trigger:* none (after initial load)
- *When:* The #boot overlay exists in index.html
- *Result:* The overlay becomes click-through immediately and api.bootDone() is invoked (boot_done command, api.ts:170). After two animation frames it fades opacity 1 to 0 over 300 ms with cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) and holds the end state (fill forwards), then is removed. A fallback removes it 600 ms after the fade is started (setTimeout called alongside animate) if onfinish does not fire. The fade uses the Web Animations API (element.animate) so the CSS clamp for Reduce Motion / Low Power Mode does not affect it. The code removes only the #boot element; the comment says it also removes the native boot box drawn behind the page, but no such removal appears in boot.ts.
- *Exact:* fade duration = `300 ms`; fade easing = `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`; fallback removal = `600 ms`; start = `after two requestAnimationFrame calls`
- *Edge cases:* Runs only once even under React StrictMode double effects
- *Status:* corrected, found by A, OS integration
- *Check notes:* Only A checked this, from source. B found no recorded animation or timing data. The boot_done command ordering matches the recorded boot sequence in main-default.
- *Sources:* main/src/lib/boot.ts:18-37, main/src/App.tsx:45-49, A: lib/boot.ts:18-37: pointerEvents none at :22; api.bootDone() at :23; double rAF at :25-26; animate opacity 1->0, duration 300, easing cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), fill forwards at :27-31; onfinish remove at :32; setTimeout(remove, 600) at :34; StrictMode guard dataset.dismissing at :20-21. **F09-065 · Switching list by clicking a tab**
- *Trigger:* click on an inactive list tab, e.g. Garden (inferred; list-switch-3 shows Garden active after set_active_list)
- *When:* Home project with Errands active. The tab-click rules are in Two panes: left (active) and split list.
- *Result:* Clicking a tab calls selectList. If the tab is already shown in either pane, it only moves focus to that pane (paneFocus). Otherwise, if a split exists and the focused pane is the split pane, the clicked list replaces the split list. Otherwise the clicked list replaces the left (active) list. The clicked tab's label turns primary and the others turn muted. The task pane changes to that list's tasks, the search placeholder becomes 'Search <list name>', and the stats bar updates. In list-switch-3 Garden shows 'Order tomato seeds' and 'Trim the hedge'. The focused list is saved with api.setActiveList, which sends the set_active_list command.
- *Exact:* active Garden label tone = `primary`; inactive label tone = `muted`; search placeholder = `Search Garden`; stats = `0/2 DONE, 0%`; command = `set_active_list`
- *Edge cases:* Clicking a tab that is already shown in a pane does not reload it into the other pane; it only focuses that pane (layoutStore.ts:86-87).
- *Status:* corrected, found by B
- *Check notes:* B's recording (list-switch-3) matches the tone, placeholder, tasks and stats. The click itself is not recorded; only the resulting set_active_list appears. A's layoutStore.ts:63 citation is imprecise ('63-ish') and was not corrected.
- *Sources:* state:list-switch-3 (tree lines 14-20, 34, 37), state:list-switch-3 (meta.json commands 32), state:list-switch-3 (screenshot), A: components/ListTabs.tsx:130 onClick={() => selectList(list.id)}; stores/layoutStore.ts:84-95 selectList rules; layoutStore.ts:63 and :63-ish persistFocus calls api.setActiveList (api.ts:148 invoke 'set_active_list'); components/TaskPane.tsx:212 placeholder `Search ${list.name}`., B: list-switch-3/tree.txt:14 Errands Label tone=muted, :17 Reading muted, :20 Garden tone=primary; :34 TaskPane list Garden; :37 TextInput2 placeholder Search Garden; :44 and :49 tasks t-seeds and t-hedge; :54 StatsBar done=0 total=2 pct=0. list-switch-3/meta.json:32 set_active_list is the last command. list-switch-3/shot.png shows Garden active, Order tomato seeds, Trim the hedge, 0/2 DONE, 0%. **F09-099 · Split list is remembered across launches in localStorage 'ui.split' and cleared by closing split, switching project, or reconciling a deleted list**
- *Trigger:* A second list is open in the split pane (toggle split, or a tab click that loads into the focused split pane), then the app is relaunched, or a project switch / list deletion happens.
- *When:* The split list id is mirrored to localStorage key 'ui.split' separately from the focused-list setting last_active_list (F09-022 covers only the focused list). On boot the initial split list is read from localStorage. reconcileLayout (bootstrap.ts) keeps it only if it is a valid list in the active project and differs from the left list; otherwise it becomes null. resetForProject and closeSplit remove the key; reconcileLists removes it when no split list remains.
- *Result:* After relaunch, if the stored list is no longer valid or equals the left list, splitListId is set to null in the store (bootstrap.ts:30-34), but the 'ui.split' localStorage key is NOT removed on that boot path. The key is only removed later by closeSplit, resetForProject, reconcileLists (when no split remains), or toggleSplit when it closes. The earlier claim 'the key is removed' is not supported for the boot path.
- *Exact:* localStorage key for the split list id = `ui.split`; Initial splitListId on store creation = `localStorage.getItem('ui.split') || null`; Validity check on load = `valid(layout.splitListId) && layout.splitListId !== activeListId, else null`; Keys removed on closeSplit, resetForProject, and reconcileLists when no split = `localStorage.removeItem('ui.split')`
- *Edge cases:* toggleSplit also removes the key when it closes the split (layoutStore.ts:105-106), and swapPanes rewrites it (layoutStore.ts:118). · reconcileLists is called only from deleteList (lists.ts:84-89).
- *Status:* corrected, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Only A could check this, and only from code. A's correction is that the boot path sets splitListId to null in the store but does not remove the 'ui.split' key. B could not check it; no conflict.
- *Sources:* main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:68, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:90, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:105-106, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:111, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:132, main/src/stores/layoutStore.ts:155, main/src/stores/bootstrap.ts:30-33, A (source, verdict corrected): layoutStore.ts:68 (splitListId from localStorage 'ui.split' || null); layoutStore.ts:90, :105-106, :111, :132, :155 (setItem and removeItem sites); bootstrap.ts:18-35 (reconcileLayout does NOT remove the key); bootstrap.ts:30-34 (validity check sets splitListId null); projects.ts:56-62 (selectProject calls resetForProject); lists.ts:84-89 (deleteList calls reconcileLists)., B (recording, verdict cannot_check): none of the nine recordings (tree.txt, meta.json, shot.png) shows localStorage or a relaunch. ## 10. Settings window (77 features)

**F10-001 · Settings window opens at a fixed 640 x 520 size and fades in after preferences and fonts load**
- *Trigger:* none (happens on open)
- *When:* Window is built fresh on each open; runs once per window
- *Result:* The content stays at opacity 0 until settings have loaded and document.fonts is ready; then the window is presented at 640 x 520 and the content plays animate-scale-in. The pane scrolls; the window does not resize.

**F10-013 · Search matching rule (AND of whitespace-separated tokens, case-insensitive)**
- *Trigger:* typing in the search field
- *When:* Applied per row across group label, row title, description and keywords
- *Result:* The query is lowercased and split on whitespace; a row matches only if every token is found as a substring in the joined haystack (group label, title, description, keywords, separated by single spaces). Groups with no matching rows are dropped.

- *Edge cases:* The group label is part of the haystack (panes.ts:16-17, :26), so a token that matches the group label, such as 'appearance', matches every row in that group. · If there are no tokens, filterGroups returns all groups unchanged (panes.ts:20). SettingsWindow never gets there, because a whitespace-only query is not searching (SettingsWindow.tsx:138).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A

- *Sources:* main/src/windows/settings/panes.ts:15-37, A: panes.ts:15-37 (tokens = query.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean) at :19; haystack order group.label, row.title, row.description ?? '', row.keywords ?? '' at :25-31; join ' ' at :31; toLowerCase :32; every token includes :33; groups with no rows dropped :36)., B: Only the single token 'motion' was recorded (settings-search/tree.txt:13), and it matched the row title 'Reduced motion' (tree.txt:29). The AND-of-tokens rule, the joined haystack order, the /\s+/ split and the case-insensitivity cannot be distinguished from this one-token example.

**F10-025 · Command-F or Ctrl-F focuses and selects the search field**

**F10-026 · Escape and Command-F are swallowed while recording a shortcut**
- *Trigger:* Escape or ⌘F pressed while a shortcut row is recording
- *When:* A shortcut row shows Type shortcut…
- *Result:* The recording handler listens in the capture phase and stops propagation, so Escape does not close the window or clear search and Cmd+F does not focus search. Escape instead cancels the recording (see its own feature).
- *Exact:* Listener phase = `capture (capture: true)`; Calls = `preventDefault and stopPropagation on every key while recording`
- *Status:* confirmed by one, found by A
- *Check notes:* A's source reading gives the capture-phase suppression. B observed a discrepancy: settings-shortcut-recording/tree.txt:49-50 shows HotkeyControl with Keycap recording=false, while the screenshot shows the 'Type shortcut…' state, and there is no HotkeyHint child. Source decides, so the capture-phase behaviour is kept, but the recording-flag discrepancy in the captured tree is noted for follow-up. Whether Escape or Cmd+F is swallowed is not recorded.
- *Sources:* main/src/windows/settings/useHotkeyEditor.ts:73-96, main/src/windows/SettingsWindow.tsx:119-120, A: useHotkeyEditor.ts:76-96 (listener only while recording, line 77; { capture: true } at :93; preventDefault and stopPropagation on every key at :79-80; Escape cancels at :81-83), SettingsWindow.tsx:119-120 (comment)., B: settings-shortcut-recording/shot.png shows the New task row with the text 'Type shortcut…' in a blue-outlined box. settings-shortcut-recording/tree.txt:49-50 show HotkeyControl @1051,238 101x21 with Keycap recording=false and no HotkeyHint child (the other rows have one). The Keycap prop reads recording=false, which does not match the visible Type shortcut… state. Whether Escape or Cmd+F is swallowed is not recorded (no key input in meta.json).

**F10-051 · Shortcut rows are searchable by their combo text**

- *Result:* The list is fetched when the window opens and re-fetched after setHotkey, resetHotkey and applyAccels calls, so the Shortcuts section reflects the stored bindings. If a fetch fails the error is ignored and the list stays empty.

**F10-055 · Values load when the settings window opens**
- *Trigger:* Open the Settings window (inferred from present_window and the state names)

**F11-001 · Reduced-motion switch is flipped from Settings and applied app-wide**
- *Trigger:* Changing the Toggle titled 'Reduced motion' in Settings > General > Appearance (generalPane.tsx:50-57; onChange at :54 calls ctx.set('reduced_motion', ...), whose write is setReducedMotion at settings.ts:35).
- *When:* Any time; applies to the window it runs in and then to other windows. Settings window, General tab, Appearance group (B recording, off).
- *Result:* The document root gets the class reduced-motion, which neutralises all CSS animations and transitions (durations 0.01ms). The new value is saved and other windows are told to match. B saw the row title and description and the toggle, recorded off (checked=false, disabled=false).
- *Exact:* setting key persisted = `reduced_motion (stored as '1' on, '0' off)`; broadcast event = `reduced-motion-changed`; root class = `reduced-motion`; Row title (B) = `Reduced motion`; Row description (B) = `Cuts animations and transitions to the minimum.`; Toggle title (B) = `Reduced motion`; Toggle size (B) = `30x18 at x=1123, y=182`; Default in recording (B) = `off (checked=false)`
- *Edge cases:* If the setting write fails, setReducedMotion rejects after the class has already been toggled locally (setPref runs before the await). The rejection is caught in settings.ts:105-112, so the user sees no error and the switch keeps the new value; the broadcast at reducedMotion.ts:57 is skipped. · Whether the value is remembered between launches is not shown in solution B's recording; solution A's source shows it is saved (see notes). · While Low Power Mode or macOS Reduce Motion forces motion, the Toggle is disabled and shown checked (generalPane.tsx:52-53; forcesMotion at :20-21).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A+B
- *Check notes:* B's exact verdict confirms the row text, the 30x18 switch and the unchecked default in the recording; A's source does not check those. A's corrected trigger and edge cases are kept. Edge case 1 refers to 'see notes', but no separate note exists in the inputs; the persistence point rests on A's settings.ts:30-35 write path. B could not see persistence.

**F12-043 · Overlay Escape to dismiss**
- *Trigger:* press Escape while an overlay is open

## 14. Capture bar, native side (63 features)

**F14-001 · Global toggle hotkey summons or dismisses the capture bar**
- *Trigger:* Press the global toggle_capture_bar combo (the default combo is defined in the common crate, not in these files). Plugin handler fires on key press only.
- *When:* The visible check runs before the main-focus check: if the bar is visible, main focus is ignored and capture-enter is emitted (lib.rs:120-132). Main-focus routing applies only when the bar is hidden (lib.rs:133-134).
- *Result:* If the bar is visible, a capture-enter event is emitted to the bar webview, which decides between submitting from the notes editor and dismissing from the title. If the bar is hidden and main is focused, POST /new-task goes to main (falls back to toggle_mini if main is unreachable). Otherwise the bar is toggled at the cursor: a hidden bar appears under the mouse cursor, a visible bar hides.
- *Exact:* default hotkey (docs) = `⌘Return = Cmd + Enter (common/src/hotkeys.rs:333, key Enter)`
- *Edge cases:* When the POST to main fails, the stale main_focused flag is cleared before the fallback runs (lib.rs:52). · On a refused OS registration the log line is "[taskscape-tray] failed to register {label} hotkey: {e}" with label capture-bar or screenshot (hotkeys.rs:174); the old registration is re-registered if that succeeds (hotkeys.rs:175). · The tray tooltip reads "Taskscape — press {glyphs} to capture", or just "Taskscape" when toggle_capture_bar is unbound (hotkeys.rs:218-221). · Hotkeys are (re)registered at startup and on POST /reload-hotkeys from main, and the tray tooltip is updated to match (doc:tray-app.md:91-94). · Global shortcut never reaches the focused bar webview, which is why the handler forwards the event.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A+B, OS integration
- *Check notes:* A corrected the visible-vs-main-focus order against lib.rs:120-134: the visible check runs first. B's docs (tray-app.md:98) have no main-focus routing or visible/hidden decision, so they add no conflicting value. B's edge cases are merged in; B's OS-refused edge case duplicates A's more exact one (hotkeys.rs:174-175), so A's wording is kept.
- *Sources:* tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:109-137, tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:43-56, doc:tray-app.md:98, doc:tray-app.md:95-96, doc:architecture.md:44, A: lib.rs:109-112 (Pressed only), 120-137 (toggle branch), 131 (capture-enter), 134 (/new-task + toggle_mini fallback), 43-55 (route_to_main_or), 204 (toggle_capture_bar), 218-222 (tooltip); default combo from common/src/hotkeys.rs:330-334 (toggle_capture_bar = Cmd + Enter, Scope::Global); OS refusal log at hotkeys.rs:173-176., B: tray-app.md:98 (toggle_capture_bar, default ⌘Return, toggle_mini), :92 (two Global-scope commands), :95-96 (only on Pressed), :105-106 (OS-refused combo logged, previous registration kept), :91-94 (registered at startup and on POST /reload-hotkeys, tooltip updated), architecture.md:44 (⌘Return shows mini bar at cursor). Not in docs: capture-enter event, POST /new-task, main-focus routing, and the visible/hidden decision.

**F14-005 · Screenshot path in region mode defers revealing a hidden bar**
- *Trigger:* Screenshot hotkey pressed while screenshot mode is region and the bar is hidden.

- *Edge cases:* A failed capture (screenshot-error path) also leaves the deferred bar hidden; the reveal runs only on a successful capture (capture.rs:124-131, 138-141). · A cancelled capture (screenshot-cancelled path) also leaves the deferred bar hidden (capture.rs:133-137).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A, OS integration
- *Check notes:* A's code (window.rs:306-313, capture.rs:124-141) confirms the deferred reveal in region mode with an extra edge case. B could not check; the docs at tray-app.md:72 and :100 state unconditionally that capture_and_show shows the bar first, which conflicts with the region-mode deferral. The code decides.
- *Sources:* tray/src-tauri/src/window.rs:297-313, tray/src-tauri/src/capture.rs:126-137, A: window.rs:306-313 (region branch: reveal_on_success = !visible, dim = visible); capture.rs:124-131 (reveal only in the Ok(Some) arm, via run_on_main_thread → reveal_mini); capture.rs:133-137 (cancel: no reveal); capture.rs:138-141 (error arm: no reveal)., B: No docs line describes a deferred reveal in region mode. tray-app.md:72 and :100 state unconditionally that capture_and_show shows the bar first if hidden, with no mode qualifier, which conflicts with this feature's claim. Unresolved.

**F14-014 · Bar is excluded from the capture itself**
- *Trigger:* Any tray-initiated capture (macOS). Docs: the bar is hidden from the tray's own shot only.
- *When:* During the grab only. The grab runs on a background thread.
- *Result:* The bar's sharing type is set to None before the grab, then the thread sleeps 60 ms so the window server commits the exclusion. The bar is restored to ReadOnly afterwards, even on error or panic, so OS tools and main can capture it again. The bar stays visible in OS screenshots (⌘⇧4) and in screenshots taken by the main app.
- *Exact:* sleep before grab = `60 ms`; exclusion sharing type = `NSWindowSharingType None (0)`; restored sharing type = `ReadOnly (1)`; block timeout = `500 ms`
- *Edge cases:* Permanent exclusion is deliberately not applied (lib.rs:182-185).
- *Status:* confirmed by both, found by A+B, OS integration
- *Check notes:* Both found the claim exact. The numeric values (0, 1, 60 ms, 500 ms) are code-only; B noted they are not in the docs and A verified them in code.
- *Sources:* tray/src-tauri/src/capture.rs:110-122, tray/src-tauri/src/capture.rs:146-160, tray/src-tauri/src/setup.rs:147-187, doc:tray-app.md:64-70, doc:tray-app.md:84-85, doc:tray-app.md:60, A: capture.rs:110-122 (set_sharing_type(false,true) → None (0); sleep 60 ms at capture.rs:120; SharingRestore to ReadOnly at capture.rs:121), capture.rs:146-160 (restore on drop, so also on error/panic), setup.rs:162-164 (None=0, ReadOnly=1), setup.rs:182-185 (block with recv_timeout 500 ms), lib.rs:182-185 (permanent exclusion deliberately not applied)., B: tray-app.md:64-67 (NSWindowSharingType flipped to None only for the grab, restored to default ReadOnly right after, even on error or panic), :68-70 (bar stays visible in ⌘⇧4 shots and main-app screenshots; hidden only from the tray's own shot), :82-85 (bar deliberately not excluded at setup), :59-60. **F14-062 · Tray hotkey routing falls back to a local mini-bar action when the main app is unreachable**
- *Trigger:* A global combo is routed to the main window (cached as frontmost) but the POST to the main port fails, for example because main was closed or crashed while frontmost.
- *When:* route_to_main_or POSTs to MAIN_PORT. On failure it clears the stale main_focused flag so later presses stop routing to a dead port, then runs the local fallback on the main thread because window operations must run there.
- *Result:* The combo still works with main gone. The tray runs its own mini-bar action and future presses are no longer routed to main until it reports focus again.
- *Exact:* Stale-cache reset on failed POST = `main_focused().store(false, Ordering::Release) before fallback(&handle) runs via app.run_on_main_thread`
- *Status:* confirmed by review, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Reviewed by Mujtaba (2026-11-13): true. Earlier check: Neither checker could verify this. A returned no verdict for this id, and B found no description of route_to_main_or, a stale main_focused flag, or a local fallback in the docs.
- *Sources:* tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:36-56, B: tray-app.md and architecture.md do not describe route_to_main_or, a stale main_focused flag, or a local fallback after a failed POST.

**F14-063 · Tray Open Taskscape launches the installed app by bundle id when no running instance answers**
- *Trigger:* Tray Open Taskscape, or the focus request, runs while the main app is not running and the POST to /focus on the main port fails.
- *When:* focus_or_launch_main_async first POSTs /focus to MAIN_PORT. If that fails it shells out to macOS open with the bundle id com.taskscape.main.app and returns false. Callers use the boolean to tell an already-running focus from a fresh launch.
- *Result:* A focus request launches the app when it is not running. The return value is false when a launch was started, not a focus.
- *Exact:* Bundle id used for launch fallback = `com.taskscape.main.app (open -b)`; Focus endpoint path posted first = `/focus on MAIN_PORT`
- *Status:* confirmed by review, found by seams
- *Check notes:* Reviewed by Mujtaba (2026-11-13): true. Earlier check: Neither checker returned a verdict for this id. B could not check it against the docs. A's F14-041 evidence cites the related code (lib.rs:79-81 focus_or_launch_main, lib.rs:63 POST /focus, lib.rs:70-71 open -b args), which overlaps with this id's claims, but A did not verdict F14-063 itself and did not mention a boolean return. Someone may need to verify it directly against the code.
- *Sources:* tray/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:58-75, B: tray-app.md:125 names the Open Taskscape item with handler focus_or_launch_main. The /focus POST, the open -b com.taskscape.main.app launch, and the boolean return are not in the docs.

**F15-005 · Import creates a new list from an exported JSON file, recreating the full tree**

- *Trigger:* Invoke copy_tasks with selected task ids (Select mode's copy action; the trigger UI lives in the frontend)

- *Result:* Each selected task becomes a line "- [ ] title" (or "- [x] title" when done). Nesting depth equals the count of selected ancestors, rendered as two spaces per level. Each non-empty note block follows its task as a blockquote line "> text" indented one level deeper than the task. **F15-044 · Note edits are saved in order by a background queue**
- *Trigger:* Typing in a note (autosave calls update_note; no visible control here)
- *When:* Autosave while typing
- *Result:* Each edit is queued (bounded at 512) and applied in arrival order by one worker so concurrent edits to one note never race; failures are only logged. The command is fire-and-forget: it awaits the queue send and returns Ok once enqueued, but when the 512-slot queue is full the send waits for space, and it returns an error only if the worker has stopped.
- *Exact:* Queue capacity = `512`
- *Edge cases:* When the queue is full, update_note blocks on send until a slot frees; it does not return immediately. · An update to a note deleted meanwhile is logged as 'queued note update failed' and skipped (lib.rs:1105-1107, 1119-1121).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* Only A checked the source. The docs do not cover the queue, so B's cannot_check does not conflict.
- *Sources:* main/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:81-85, main/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:545-554, main/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:953, main/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:1105-1123, A: Capacity 512: lib.rs:953 channel::<(String,String)>(512), rationale lib.rs:949-952. Single worker: lib.rs:1108-1123. Arrival order: lib.rs:1118 while let recv. Failures logged only: lib.rs:1119-1121. update_note: lib.rs:545-554 does queue.0.send((id, content)).await.map_err(err)., B (cannot_check): update_note is not in the main-app.md commands list (main-app.md:22-26). No doc describes autosave, the 512-entry queue, or the background worker.

**F17-039 · Canonical accelerator string form**
- *Trigger:* none (stored and sent format)
- *When:* Used for IPC payloads and stored overrides.

Example test hotkeys.rs:689-690 ("Cmd+Alt+Shift+K"). Modifier names are matched case-sensitively (257-260), and malformed input is rejected: two keys (263-265), missing key (269), and test cases "Cmd+Shft+K", "Cmd+K+J", "Cmd" (hotkeys.rs:697-712)., .llm/common-crate.md:11 confirms a 'canonical accel format' exists, but gives no modifier order, token form or example such as Cmd+Alt+Shift+K.

- *Sources:* doc:common-crate.md:33-36, common/src/storage.rs:609-625 (connect): journal_mode(SqliteJournalMode::Wal) line 617; busy_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)) line 618; foreign_keys(true) line 619; max_connections(4) line 621; comment lines 609-610 says every connection gets these settings. doc:common-crate.md:33-36 not opened., common-crate.md:33-36 says the SQLx pool sets journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout=5s, foreign_keys=ON on every connection, and max_connections = 4 (line 33). The doc says foreign_keys=ON is required for ON DELETE CASCADE. It does not say 'before failing'. architecture.md:35 says both apps share the DB.

**F17-078 · Migrations applied at startup and data preserved**
- *Trigger:* none (observed on app launch after a schema change)
- *When:* App launch with unapplied migrations
- *Result:* At startup, every migration file whose version (file stem, e.g. 20260709090335_baseline) is not in schema_migrations is replayed in filename order, each in its own transaction together with its schema_migrations insert (migrations.rs:45-75). Versions are Atlas timestamp-prefixed, not 0002-style numbers.
- *Exact:* migration table = `schema_migrations`
- *Edge cases:* The data-preservation rule ("from 0002 on") is a CLAUDE.md guideline; no code checks it, and no 0002 file exists in common/migrations.
- *Status:* corrected, found by B
- *Check notes:* Both checkers agree that migrations are recorded in schema_migrations and replayed in a transaction at startup. Checker A's corrections give the code-level detail (Atlas timestamp-prefixed versions, filename order, per-migration transaction). Checker B's doc citations (common-crate.md:15, :39-41) support this. B noted that common-crate.md:60 is about gen-entities.sh, not data preservation, and that the 'from 0002 on must preserve data' rule is in CLAUDE.md Gotchas. A's edge case already records that the rule is a CLAUDE.md guideline with no code enforcement and no 0002 file, so B's sourcing point is merged into that edge case rather than duplicated.
- *Sources:* doc:common-crate.md:39-41, doc:common-crate.md:60, common/src/migrations.rs:1-8, 23-25 (versions are Atlas sortable UTC timestamp filenames); migrations.rs:26-33 (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (version TEXT PRIMARY KEY, applied_at INTEGER NOT NULL)); migrations.rs:45-60 (*.sql in filename order, skip applied); migrations.rs:65-75 (each migration in its own transaction, version row inserted in same txn); Glob of common/migrations: 20260709090335_baseline.sql, 20260713135048_drop_settings.sql, 20260713143924_add_task_deleted_at.sql. No 0002 file exists. CLAUDE.md states "Migrations from 0002 on must preserve data" as a repo rule, not enforced in code., common-crate.md:39-41 says migrations.rs records applied versions in schema_migrations and replays new ones in a transaction at startup. common-crate.md:15 says it applies unrecorded versions at startup. common-crate.md:60 is about regenerating entities with gen-entities.sh, not migration data preservation. The claim 'migrations from 0002 on must preserve data' is stated in CLAUDE.md (Gotchas section, provided in context), not in the two named docs.

**F18-001 · Task row click previews the task**

Both trees show picked=false and the empty preview state (main-dark/tree.txt:95-96).

- *Edge cases:* The Check element carries both onToggleDone and onToggleSelect handler props (main-dark/tree.txt:45), so the prop list alone does not show which handler a click calls. · The recording shows picked=false on every row. - *Status:* corrected, found by A+B
- *Check notes:* Both checkers agree on the select handle behaviour. B's verdict is corrected only through edge notes: the element is named Check in the tree, not checkbox, and the click result is not recorded because meta.json has no click. No value conflict, so A's source result stands.
- *Sources:* docs/main-app-design-review-2026-08-13.md:24, docs/main-app-design-review-2026-08-13.md:53, docs/main-app-design-review-2026-08-13.md:177, main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:493, state:main-dark tree.txt line 45, state:main-dark tree.txt line 51, state:main-dark tree.txt line 56, A: main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:493-498 (default round select handle, picked row fills accent); TaskRow.tsx:510-520 (title 'Select' / 'Deselect' when not in Option mode); TaskRow.tsx:535-536 (click without altKey calls onToggleSelect); TaskRow.tsx:380 (onToggleSelect wired to paneToggleSelect). **F18-003 · Option-held checkbox turns into a done control**

**F18-004 · Double-click on a task row marks it done**
- *Trigger:* Double-click a task row
- *When:* Task list
- *Result:* Double-click on the row calls toggleDone(), which toggles the task's done state. It marks a done task as not done too. Double-clicking the round checkbox does not toggle done (the checkbox stops propagation). Keyboard behaviour follows the same select/done split: Space toggles selection and Option+Space marks done (or toggles done for the active task).
- *Edge cases:* Double-click on an expand chevron (TaskRow.tsx:420) or on the checkbox (TaskRow.tsx:538) does not toggle done.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* Conflict on where the double-click handler sits. B saw onDoubleClick on the More IconButton (main-dark/tree.txt:48, and lines 53, 58, 63, 70, 75, 80, 85), not on the TaskRow2 root (tree.txt:44, which lists only taskId and depth). A's source (TaskRow.tsx:335-338, row onDoubleClick calling stopPropagation then toggleDone) decides the result. No double-click was performed, so the marks-done result is unchecked by B.
- *Sources:* docs/main-app-design-review-2026-08-13.md:53, docs/main-app-design-review-2026-08-13.md:54, main/src/hooks/useAppKeyboard.ts:40, A: main/src/components/TaskRow.tsx:335-338 (onDoubleClick calls e.stopPropagation() then toggleDone()); TaskRow.tsx:538 (checkbox stops double-click propagation); main/src/hooks/useAppKeyboard.ts:263-281 (Space toggles selection, Option+Space marks done)., B: main-dark/tree.txt:44 shows TaskRow2 taskId="t-pharmacy" depth=0 with no onDoubleClick; main-dark/tree.txt:48 shows IconButton icon="more_horiz" title="More" onDoubleClick=ƒ. No double-click performed.

## 19. Command surface (73 features)

**F19-001 · Relative time shows "just now" for under 45 seconds**
- *Trigger:* none (display helper; no user action in these files)
- *When:* Any timestamp rendered through relativeTime(ms)
- *Result:* A timestamp less than 45 seconds old is shown as "just now".
- *Exact:* label = `just now`; threshold = `sec < 45 (sec = Math.round(diff / 1000))`
- *Edge cases:* Uses Date.now() at call time, so the label is not live-updated by this file. · The cutoff applies to the rounded value, so a diff below 44,500 ms shows "just now" (time.ts:4-5). · A future timestamp gives a negative diff and sec, which is below 45, so it also shows "just now" (time.ts:3-5).
- *Status:* corrected, found by A
- *Check notes:* Checker A verified against source. Checker B could not check (docs silent). Source decides.
- *Sources:* main/src/time.ts:2-5, main/src/time.ts:2-5 (diff line 3, sec = Math.round(diff/1000) line 4, sec < 45 check line 5), Checked .llm/common-crate.md and conventions.md in full. Neither mentions relativeTime, the "just now" label, or the 45-second threshold. common-crate.md:20 only covers util::now_millis() (Rust unix millis), not the frontend helper.

**F19-002 · Relative time shows minutes ago**
- *Trigger:* none (display helper)
- *When:* Timestamp at least 45 seconds old and under 60 minutes old
- *Result:* Shown as whole minutes followed by " ago".

**F19-043 · Hotkey catalog, rebinding, and reset; conflicting bindings are rejected**
- *Trigger:* none (command wrapper; keybinding UI outside this area)
- *When:* Viewing or changing keyboard shortcuts
- *Result:* listHotkeys returns the catalog with effective (user-customized) combos (resolve). setHotkey(id, accel) validates and persists an accelerator for a command id; an empty accel unbinds it. resetHotkey(id) drops the user override and restores the default combo. The backend rejects: an unknown id, an unparseable accelerator, a bare key without ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥ (F-keys are exempt), and a combo already used by another command in the same scope, with the message already used by “<label of holder>”. Assigning the command's own default removes the override.

- *Edge cases:* Conflict check applies only to commands in the same scope (hotkeys.rs:610-612). · The rejection message text is found: hotkeys.rs:608 and 612. · common-ui/src/hotkeys.ts was not opened, so the frontend twin is not verified here.
- *Status:* corrected, found by A+B, OS integration
- *Check notes:* A and B agree on the underlying functions (resolve, set_binding; canonical accel format). B's gaps (no docs for the command names, reset, or rejection text) are not conflicts; A's source-based values stand. The frontend twin in common-ui/src/hotkeys.ts was not checked by A.
